title: Increasing Subsequence Length
summary: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. Implement `increasing_subsequence_length` and return the required result without changing the callable signature.
constraints: Inputs follow the declared Python and JSON-compatible types.
Return a deterministic result for every valid input.
hints: Smallest possible tail values leave the most room for future extension.
Binary-search the first tail not smaller than each value and replace it.
Pseudocode checkpoint: identify the state, update it once per step, and return only after the increasing_subsequence_length invariant is complete.
Editorial: Binary-search the first tail not smaller than each value and replace it. The intended bounds are O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
editorial: Smallest possible tail values leave the most room for future extension. Binary-search the first tail not smaller than each value and replace it. This yields O(n log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

tests.explanation: A longest increasing subsequence such as [2, 3, 7, 18] has length 4.
A decreasing list has a longest increasing subsequence of one value.
